label: Luis D. Elizondo
narrative: Elizondo is the witness who put the contractor divestment attempt on the congressional record under oath. On 13 November 2024, before the House Oversight Committee, Rep. Eric Burlison asked him whether defense contractors possess technology. Elizondo answered that his predecessor program AAWSAP had tried to collect 'material of unknown origin,' that 'there was an aerospace contract company that requested to divest itself of the material... that was collected in the 1950s,' and that the transfer did not occur. Burlison then read to him the reporting of journalist Christopher Sharp describing a transfer between Lockheed Martin, Bigelow Aerospace and a CIA block; Elizondo replied 'What I can say is that it was blocked,' said he had later been told by contract personnel that the account was accurate, and explained the bureaucratic mechanism: the transfer required a memorandum from the Secretary of the Air Force that never came, after which he attempted to obtain one from Secretary of Defense James Mattis instead. Asked who possesses the material today, he refused to answer in open session. In the same hearing, Rep. Nancy Mace asked whether material is allocated to contractors by domain expertise - undersea propulsion to a General Dynamics, aerospace to Lockheed - and Elizondo replied 'Yes, ma'am, absolutely correct. Different contractors have different levels of expertise.' That exchange is the clearest description in any public record of how a distributed contractor custody architecture would function. Elizondo's statements are pre-publication-reviewed by DoD's Office of Prepublication and Security Review, a point he made in the hearing itself.

timeline.label: Elizondo assumes AATIP role
timeline.text: On TTSA's account Elizondo takes over AATIP as Director in 2010, running it from OUSD(I). Neill Tipton, his superior in this period, later states he brought no AATIP responsibilities with him.

timeline.label: 'Exemplary' performance evaluation
timeline.text: Elizondo's annual evaluation rates him exemplary; his supervisor writes that it 'cannot be overstated the importance of Mr. Elizondo's portfolio to national security' and credits him with neutralising six insider threats.

timeline.label: 60 Minutes segment
timeline.text: Elizondo, Mellon and Navy aviators appear in a CBS 60 Minutes report on UAP in restricted U.S. airspace, weeks before the ODNI preliminary assessment.

timeline.label: Elizondo's claimed 600-1,000-foot disc identified as an irrigation circle
timeline.text: At a UAP Disclosure Fund hearing Luis Elizondo presents an image described as a gigantic disc; analysts including Mick West identify it as an irrigation circle. The correction comes from the sceptic community, not the government.
